did: Typed 'Ney, attack Mack' after the muster listed Davout, Lannes, Murat joining
expected: Some warning that marching four corps into Swabia would turn my income from +828/turn to +13/turn
saw: Header showed '800 (+828 next turn)'; after the battle it read '133 (+13 next turn)'. Only the Economy ledger explains it (Campaign pay -1188g for corps fed on allied soil, Over-limit surcharge, Grande Armee surcharge). The muster card warns about materiel losses but not about campaign pay for the reinforcing corps.

did: Accepted Saxony's (and earlier Portugal's) Open Borders letter, whose terms line said 'Offer: Gold payment - 82' (and '- 60' for Portugal)
expected: Either my treasury to rise by that sum, or the letter to say plainly who pays whom and when
saw: Treasury stayed 244 (and stayed 105 after Portugal). The confirmation line only says 'Treaty signed: Peace -> Open Borders'. The sum is never mentioned again, so I cannot tell if I was paid, if I will be, or if it is a cost.

did: After accepting Saxony's Open Borders letter (Offer: Gold payment - 82), opened the Admiralty book
expected: The treasury shown in the command panel and the Admiralty to agree
saw: Command panel still says Gold: 244 (+458 next turn); the Admiralty book says 'the treasury holds 326g'. So the 82g was paid to me, but the Gold line was not refreshed after the treaty (it stayed 244 through the Portugal letter too, where I presumably also got 60). Updating the earlier row: the payment IS received, the header just does not show it.

did: Read the muster ('what if Ney attacks Archduke Charles': expect about 118,448, Massena 99% likely, Davout 76%, Lannes 98%) and then ordered 'Ney, attack Archduke Charles'
expected: A favourable fight roughly as the muster described (118k vs 41k)
saw: Only 52,597 took the field: Davout 'could not reach the battlefield', Massena 'was nearly in position, but fate intervened at the crucial moment' (a 99% corps), Murat did not arrive. Result a 'brutal stalemate' (Ney 19.5k->17k, Charles 41k->35k) and a treasury of 77g. The 'expect about 118,448' headline is the sum of everybody who MIGHT come, not an expectation; a 99% corps and a 76% corps both missing is hard to believe. I committed a turn's action on a number that was off by more than half.

did: With the camp already 'Staged: 40,000 men have stood 2 turns in the camp' (Flanders), ordered 'Soult, march to Normandy' and 'Napoleon, march to Normandy' (a camp province) to be ready to cross
expected: To stay in the camp, or at least to be warned: both Flanders and Normandy are named camp provinces
saw: The order's route was 'Picardy -> Artois -> Normandy' and the first step moved both onto Picardy, which is not a camp province. The Admiralty then read 'No army is staged: 0 of the 40,000 men a descent requires stand in the camp', so I threw away the two turns of staging (and the promised blockade lift). Nothing on the order's reply or card warned that the first step leaves the camp, and the route avoids the direct Flanders-Artois step.

did: Typed 'Massena, march to Milan' (a plain move, to send him home to cover Italy) while my armistice proposal to Austria was still travelling
expected: A march to a friendly city, with the route shown to me first (as it was for Soult: 'Route: Picardy -> Artois -> Normandy')
saw: 'Massena: Archduke John bars the way! Engaging!' - the path to Milan ran through enemy-held Tyrol, so the move became a full attack I never ordered; Ney, Davout, Lannes, Murat and Teulie were then pulled in by the corps system and all stand at Tyrol; Europe's alarm +8 (threat 89 -> 97/100), 1,691 men lost to the march, materiel paid, all with an armistice offer pending. Berthier said nothing about the route before the order ran. A move order whose route enters an enemy province should stop and ask, not fight.

did: Clicked 'Continue as Ordered' on Massena's interrupt; the log said 'Massena arrives at Milan'
expected: The morning dispatch printed straight after to show Massena at Milan
saw: The Morning Dispatch printed right below says 'Massena - Tyrol - HALTED at Tyrol - awaiting your word', 'Starving - supply has failed at Tyrol' and 'Massena and Teulie stand 31,319 men at Tyrol', while the map and the log show him at Milan. The dispatch was built before my answer to the interrupt and shown after it, so it reads as stale/contradictory.

did: Landed Dumonceau at Munster (Ireland) and chose SECURE
expected: The Active Wars panel to keep reading 'War with the Third Coalition' and for Ireland to be called Ireland (the province is named Munster and its owner 'Britain')
saw: The panel header changed to 'War for Munster' (listed twice: once for the whole war, once as 'War for Munster - Austria, truce 4t'), so my war with Britain/Russia/Austria is now named after one Irish province and the Austria truce line carries the wrong name. Nothing tells me whether Ireland is 'free', who rules Munster, or what the next step to raise Ireland is.

did: Typed 'Murat, cancel' to stop his march order (the game had told me for Ney: 'Ney, cancel' recalls him)
saw: Berthier: 'I cannot determine the order. Perhaps Murat, attack Moore or Murat, move to Paris?' - no help that 'halt' or 'stop' is the word. 'Murat, halt' worked (1 AP). Also earlier 'lay down two ships' laid exactly one keel with no remark that the 2 was ignored (reply just said '1 more keel possible').

did: Ordered 'The Grand Diversion' at readiness 75 after the card said: '50 times in 100 the strait opens for 2 turns; otherwise she is caught coming home and fights at readiness 65. She may try it again 4 turns from now'
expected: A failure to cost me something I could weigh - a cooldown, a readiness hit - the way a failed landing is priced (~30% of the corps lost)
saw: The 50% that failed was a fleet action: 'A decisive defeat' - France 49 -> 25 sail, Spain 33 -> 17, Holland 12 -> 6, Britain only 100 -> 96. Half my navy (and my allies' navies) gone on a coin flip whose downside was never stated as sail lost. The Admiralty page lists the odds and the 4-turn cooldown but not 'a failure destroys about half the fleet'. I would not have ordered it blind at 50/50 had it said so.

did: Wanted to start 'Improve Relations' with Britain after the armistice
expected: Talleyrand free: the Austria mission was meant to end with the peace (turn 10)
saw: The Austria mission silently kept running for 4 more turns at 1 DP a turn (Austria went from -80 to -13, well past the -60 needed for peace), and it blocked a new mission ('Mission already active'). Typing 'recall Talleyrand' got a pointer to 'F1 -> the court -> Cancel'; I had to scroll the long Cabinet list to find Austria among the Treaties to press 'Cancel: Improve Relations'. Nothing on the screen said the mission was still running except the top-bar chip 'Talleyrand: Improving Relations...'.

did: Held Munster (Ireland) from turn 6, then ratified Britain's offered white peace on turn 15 because it said 'Munster stays ours by the treaty - titled'
expected: To be told that raising Ireland (my road) needed more than Munster, and that this peace would close the door
saw: Only now, in Cabinet -> Formable Nations, do I read: 'Ireland - client state at the settlement table: at war with Britain; Ulster held at the settlement table (currently Britain-held); Munster held'. Ulster was never named anywhere I looked - the Admiralty's landing chips only listed Wales/Midlands/Northumbria/Cornwall, the Munster panel, the war panel and the peace review did not mention it. The peace review listed only 'Status quo: Munster stays ours', so I traded away the Free-Ireland road for a province without warning. The whole road should surface its next step (take Ulster, then carve at the table) where the Irish landing is made and in the peace review.

did: Read the Coalition Threat line of the Morning Dispatch on turns 19 and 20
expected: The count of quiet turns to rise by one
saw: Turn 19: 'Europe has watched us 6 quiet turns. At this pace the courts consult on turn 35 and declare on turn 38'. Turn 20: 'Europe has watched us 16 quiet turns... consult on turn 26 and declare on turn 29' - and the same dispatch's opening line says '4 more quiet turns and the courts re-arm'. The count jumped by ten and the projected dates moved nine turns closer in a single turn with no explanation.
